author: Paolo Barbero (revised from AdeptiCon tournament missions)

title: The Road to Hell
forces: Up to 1250 points per fleet (framework p.5), official fleet list, at least one cruiser or battleship.
summary: Two semi-stable warp rifts lie 30cm either side of the table centre. Fleets deploy alternately within 30cm of the long edges. Ships fully within 20cm of a rift at the end of their movement may 'board' it to deploy a Rift Stabilizer; the action always succeeds.
special_rules: Deploy Rift Stabilizers: boarding action against a warp rift from within 20cm, always successful (escort squadrons count as a multi-ship boarding action)

xr_conflicts.xr_text: have each player roll a number of D6 equal to their fleet's attack rating and choose the best individual dice score
xr_conflicts.effect: The source rolls one die and adds the attack rating. Under XR the attack rating is the number of dice. The two methods favour high-rating fleets very differently (a Corsair Eldar fleet adds 4 to one die instead of taking the best of four).

xr_conflicts.source_text: Sub-plots, Adeptus Mechanicus' Quest for Knowledge included, are not active.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: each player (starting with the attacker) may choose whether or not to generate a sub-plot.
xr_conflicts.effect: The framework (1250pt limit, Battle Points, no sub-plots) is a tournament layer outside XR. Outside a tournament the supplement would need a decision on whether to keep it.

xr_conflicts.xr_section: s.5 Fleet Commanders; booklet ruling on Bridge Smashed
xr_conflicts.source_text: If the ship an Admiral is appointed to suffers a Bridge Smashed critical hit, the Admiral counts as having been killed for all Secondary Objectives tied the Admiral's demise or survival.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Fleet commander re-rolls are lost if the commander's ship suffers Bridge Smashed or is destroyed.
xr_conflicts.effect: Compatible in spirit. XR calls the character a fleet commander, not an Admiral. The framework applies to the Secondary Objectives only; VP for the commander's ship follow s.38 as normal.

xr_conflicts.source_text: ships fully within 20 cm of a Warp Rift are allowed to declare a boarding action against it in order to deploy a Stabilizer
xr_conflicts.xr_text: To initiate a boarding action, the owning player must begin by moving the attacking vessel into base contact with the target and declaring the intent to board.
xr_conflicts.effect: XR boarding needs base contact with a ship and a troop rating contest. A rift is not a ship and the source needs no contact. The source overrides the XR rule for this one use, so the supplement would state it as a special rule and drop troop ratings.

xr_conflicts.xr_text: Warp rifts are D3x5cm wide and D3x10cm long.
xr_conflicts.effect: The source gives no rift size; the diagram shows two equal rifts. Navigation tests and destruction of ordnance follow XR unchanged.

xr_conflicts: Checked and no conflict: first turn roll-off (s.2), alternate deployment, gas clouds and asteroid fields (s.39), VP (s.38), game length (time limit allowed by s.2 'Ending the battle').
missing_or_unclear: Rift size is not stated (the diagram shows both rifts the same size).
What a deployed Stabilizer does after deployment is not stated; it only earns +4 BP.
'Semi-stable': whether stabilised rifts stop being a hazard to navigation is not stated, so XR warp rift tests are assumed to continue.
Whether a ship can board a rift it has already stabilised.
notes: Two-player symmetric. Secondary Objectives (Battle Points): +4 deploy one or more Rift Stabilizers; +2 completely destroy a capital ship or escort squadron; +2 kill the enemy Admiral or the Admiral disengages. VP as normal. Original: Tournament Mission Pack A2 (AdeptiCon 2007).

forces: Up to 1250 points per fleet. The Research Station is free (macrobattery 30cm FP10 all round, lance 30cm FP4 all round).
